intro: Leucine is an amino acid that helps trigger muscle protein synthesis. You do not need to obsess over milligrams — you need meals that naturally deliver enough high-quality protein.
buddyTip: When choosing a protein, ask: “Is this a real portion of a leucine-rich food — or a sprinkle?”
mission: Build one meal around a leucine-rich protein (dairy, eggs, fish, meat, or a well-planned soy option) and log the portion.
why: Muscle does not only care that “some protein” appeared today. A sufficient per-meal dose of essential amino acids — leucine among them — helps signal repair and growth, especially alongside training and aging.

This is why a yoghurt with 5g protein and a cottage-cheese bowl with 30g protein are not interchangeable coaching advice. The second is more likely to cross a practical leucine threshold for that meal.
kCal Buddy talks about leucine because food quality is part of ground truth. Equal calories and even similar protein grams can differ in amino acid profile and real-world effect.

points: Animal proteins and dairy are typically leucine-dense per calorie
Soy can be a strong plant option; many other plants need larger portions or combining
Per-meal protein targets usually take care of leucine without tracking it directly
Spreading 3–4 protein-containing meals beats one late spike for most people
Supplements are optional tools — food patterns come first

misconceptions.myth: I must buy leucine pills to make progress.
misconceptions.truth: Most people meet needs by eating adequate high-quality protein portions. Pills are niche, not a prerequisite.

misconceptions.myth: Any protein bar with “25g protein” is automatically leucine-optimal.
misconceptions.truth: Check actual protein quality and how you feel. Some bars are candy with a protein claim — still fine occasionally, not a daily strategy.

how.lead: Use leucine as a lens on meal design, not a new spreadsheet column.
steps: Choose protein foods you enjoy and can repeat
Aim for a satisfying protein portion at breakfast and lunch — not only dinner
On plant-forward days, increase portion size or include soy/dairy if it fits your pattern
Around training, include a normal protein-rich meal or snack within your routine
Log honestly so weekly Progress reflects real protein consistency
how.buddyHelps: Buddy emphasises protein-forward meals and teaching moments about food quality. You coach plates; Buddy keeps the diary and trends honest.

sections.title: Aging and training
paras: Older adults often need more intentional per-meal protein to stimulate muscle protein synthesis. Leucine-aware meal design is practical longevity work.
Lifters benefit too — but recovery, total energy, and sleep still matter. Leucine is one signal, not a magic switch.

sections.title: Simple food examples
paras: Eggs, skyr/quark, cottage cheese, milk-based proteins, fish, poultry, lean meats, and tofu/tempeh are common building blocks.
Build the meal around that block, then add fibre-rich plants and smart carbs/fats for the rest of your budget.

mistakes.quote: I sprinkled cheese on salad for leucine.
mistakes.why: Sprinkles rarely hit a useful per-meal dose. Use a proper protein portion.

mistakes.quote: I’ll just mega-dose whey at night and eat low protein all day.
mistakes.why: One spike does not fully replace distributed meals for hunger or frequent MPS signals.

mistakes.quote: Leucine means I can ignore total calories.
mistakes.why: Amino acid quality sits on top of energy balance — it does not replace it.

encouragement: You do not need a lab notebook. You need satisfying protein portions most meals. That is leucine strategy in real life.
